MRK.rationale: MRK presents an extremely unattractive risk-reward profile as of 2026-06-05. The Q1 2026 earnings collapse (net income -$4.24B, EPS -$1.72, operating income -$3.53B) represents a severe negative inflection, with the operating income swing from Q1 2025's +$5.90B to Q1 2026's -$3.53B — a ~$9.4B deterioration. Critically, the cause of this loss remains unexplained by the evidence: the Terns acquisition charge (~$5.8B) was announced May 13, 2026, after Q1 period-end (March 31), so it is unlikely to be the driver, leaving the loss source opaque. Gross margins remain healthy at ~74%, confirming the issue is below the gross-profit line. The stock at $120.26 is within 4% of its 251-bar high of $125.14 while trailing PE has mechanically expanded to 33.3x — the ceiling of its 365-day range (11.1–33.9x) and more than double the prior 11–15x norm. Earnings yield of 3.0% sits 147bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47%, offering no equity risk premium. Balance sheet is deteriorating: equity fell from $51.91B to $45.93B, liabilities rose to $82.75B. The Keytruda patent cliff (~late 2028/2029) remains the defining structural risk, with Keytruda family accounting for ~$8B of Q1 revenue (~49% of total). Gardasil declined 22% in Q1, adding near-term headwinds. While operating cash flow of $3.92B (+56.7% YoY) and revenue growth of +4.9% are genuine positives, they cannot compensate for a valuation that prices in recovery while the most recent data shows deterioration and the loss driver is unidentified. The market appears to have not fully processed the Q1 loss given sentiment averaging 0.603. All three pillars — deteriorating fundamentals, extreme valuation vs. own history, and absence of a credible near-term re-rating catalyst — align negatively.
